# Climate portfolio pricing: grid financing, credit redesign, bill protection and disaster preparedness

*Generated by `index/tools/climate-portfolio/pricing.py` from `pricing.json`; do not edit by hand. Read with [climate-portfolio-allocation.md](climate-portfolio-allocation.md) and [climate-portfolio-disaster-resilience.md](climate-portfolio-disaster-resilience.md). Ranges are low / mid / high; 2025 dollars unless marked.*

## Whole-package budget by account, with annual paths

Package A (with the approved $150-by-2037 price) plus the core and fuller disaster tiers, nominal $B. Four cases pair savings and costs consistently: **favorable** (credit savings x1.33, low costs) / **central** / **conservative** (credit savings x0.67, the project rule until scored; central costs) / **unfavorable** (credit savings x0.67, high costs). Negative is a saving. Removal purchases (CLI-13) are kept outside the package and shown separately.

**Accounts.** *General fund* items are paid without borrowing. *D4-B borrowing* covers time-limited capital. The *carbon channel* covers clean-industry contracts and forests, financed first from the transition share (20%) of the added REV-C1 receipts. Under D7 the dividend takes 80% and the general fund books a 25% income and payroll tax offset (CX). D7: REV-C1 receipts split 80% Climate Dividend and 20% transition share; the general fund books a 25% income and payroll tax offset (CX) on carbon fees. Added receipts from the higher price and process coverage follow the same rule unless Espen changes it.

## Paying for the package: options

Each option applies to the package's increment over the decided package (the $150 path is already in the shared ledger). General fund is nominal $B, favorable / central / conservative / unfavorable; a negative is a saving. The dividend columns are the change against D7 per consumer unit, central case, nominal dollars, lowest to highest quintile (adults per unit 1.3 / 1.7 / 2.0 / 2.2 / 2.4). The $150 step's own transition share (about $93B over 2030-39 in the model) is already credited to CLI-5 in the shared ledger (CLI-5's own revenue is 20% of REV-C1 plus REV-C2 and REV-C3), so no option spends it again; O4, which did, is withdrawn. Options O2, O3 and O5 change how D7's split applies to new receipts, so they are Espen's.

**Proposed: O5** (decided by Espen, Oct 27 ("approve O5 and CLI-7C"); Codex books it with Package A). O5 is the only option that leaves the package at or below zero for the general fund in FY2040 and FY2050 in all four cases, so the package's permanent pieces (disaster D2-D8, farm payments, bill protection) are paid at maturity by the fee that causes them. It costs households far less than O3: process receipts leave the dividend only in years the package would otherwise draw on the general fund. O2 barely moves the general fund. O3 raises more but takes about $90-170 a year from each quintile's dividend over 2030-39. Under O5 the combustion fee keeps D7's 80/20 split untouched. Corrected after review (Oct 26): an earlier O5 also spent the $150 step's transition share, which the shared ledger already credits to CLI-5; without it O5 still meets the maturity test but its 2030-39 result is about +$21B (central), not -$68B.

**Removal purchases, outside the package.** About 20 / 45 / 90 $B (2025 dollars) over 2030-39, rising to roughly 60 / 90 / 120 $B a year by 2050 at 150 / 300 / 400 Mt. That continuing obligation needs its own financing decision and maturity test before it enters any selected package.

## Grid financing windows

Budget cost under the Federal Credit Reform Act counts grants in full, direct loans at their subsidy cost and contracts at expected net cost. "Gross financing" is what Treasury borrows to make the program work, much of it repaid. Loan repayments fall on transmission charges, shown as a bill effect at 899 kWh a month before system savings; the DOE National Transmission Planning Study finds $1.60-1.80 of system cost saved per $1 of transmission, so the net bill effect is likely a saving (not banked).

| Variant | Grants / loans / contracts ($B) | Budget (deficit) cost, $B | Physical build enabled, $B | Gross Treasury financing, $B | Loan repayment on bills, $/month | System savings to 2050, $B (not banked) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| All appropriated (the earlier proposal) | 120 / 0 / 0 | 120 / 120 / 120 | 120 | 120 | 0.00 | 192 / 216 |
| Lean tranche 1 (recommended first) | 25 / 100 / 20 | 28 / 32 / 40 | 165 | 129 | 1.23 | 264 / 297 |
| Full program if tranche 1 delivers | 40 / 200 / 40 | 46 / 54 / 70 | 320 | 248 | 2.45 | 512 / 576 |

Windows:
- **Federal construction and grants: lines no regional builder will build, reconductoring on federal power-marketing systems, plan-selected interregional segments** (budget authority, mandatory, available until expended). 
- **Direct loan authority: a TVA-model federal transmission corporation, TVA, BPA, WAPA, public power and co-ops, at Treasury rates for 30-40 years, repaid from transmission charges** (direct loans under the Federal Credit Reform Act (subsidy cost scored)). estimate: subsidy rates for regulated, cost-of-service-backed lending are low single digits; BPA's Treasury borrowing authority is $13.7B rising to $17.7B in FY2028 and TVA's statutory debt cap is $30B (unchanged since 1979)
- **Capacity contract authority: DOE buys up to half of an anchor line's capacity for 10-20 years and resells it (Transmission Facilitation Program model, expanded)** (contract authority backed by the Judgment Fund; expected net cost scored at obligation). estimate; the Transmission Facilitation Program's $2.5B revolving authority was nearly depleted after two rounds (DOE, Oct 2024), and two developers have since terminated agreements

## Credit redesign in ledger terms

Credit outlays in the model (credits less grid-program cost, plus the industrial-support estimate), $T nominal 2030-39. Ledger scaling factor 0.75 (ledger CLI-1A $0.90T plus CLI-5 transmission ITC and 45X about $0.22T, against the model's $1.49T for the same credit set in 2030-39 (index/climate-carbon-model.md)).

| Package | Model credit outlays, $T nominal 2030-39 |
| --- | --- |
| decided | 1.495 |
| decided_standard_led | 0.795 |
| recommended_keep_credits | 2.191 |
| recommended | 1.141 |
| decided_old100 | 1.490 |

- Standard-led redesign alone (decided package otherwise): -0.700T in the model; in ledger terms -0.35 / -0.53 / -0.70T.
- Inside the recommended package (against the same package with credits kept): -1.050T in the model. Stronger standards raise credit claims if credits are kept, so the redesign saves more inside the package.
- Recommended package credit outlays against the decided package: -0.354T in the model; in ledger terms -0.18 / -0.27 / -0.35T.
These are estimates on the model's take-up, not a JCT score; count the low end in D4 tests until scored.

## Bill protection

Offsetting the recommended package's residential bill increase for low- and moderate-income households over 2033-39 costs 5.1 / 5.5 / 5.9 $B (2025 dollars), 0.007 / 0.007 / 0.008 $T nominal. Annual increase per household: 2033 $5, 2034 $8, 2035 $8, 2036 $12, 2037 $18, 2038 $24, 2039 $24.

## Disaster preparedness and response package

Starting from current law (sourced):

- Disaster assistance appropriations, all agencies, FY2015-24: at least $448B (about $45B a year nominal) (GAO-25-108125)
- Disaster Relief Supplemental Appropriations Act, 2025 (Dec 2024): $110B (GAO-25-108125)
- FEMA Disaster Relief Fund, FY2026: $26.4B (reported; not confirmed against enacted text) (GAO-26-108427 as cited in sources/capacity-recovery-components.csv)
- FEMA spending, 30-year average: about $12B a year (2022 dollars), $2B (1992) to $47B (2020) (CBO publication 58840)
- NFIP debt to Treasury: $22.525B, $7.9B borrowing authority left; authorization to Sept 30, 2026 after 35 short-term extensions since FY2017 (CRS IN10784 (March 2026))
- Wildfire appropriations, Forest Service and Interior, FY2025: $7.3B (CRS IF13102)
- FEMA workforce: 25,134 (FY2025) to 20,968 (April 2026) (GAO-26-108427 as cited in sources/capacity-recovery-components.csv)
- BRIC: Cancelled April 2025; ruled unlawful Dec 2025; FEMA said in March 2026 it would release remaining funds and open up to $1B of applications (Massachusetts AG; NC DOJ)
- FEMA Review Council final report (May 7, 2026): Parametric block grant for Public Assistance, a single survivor payment, higher declaration thresholds, shift flood insurance toward states and private market; most needs Congress (CRS IN12693; NACo)

A current-law exposure, not an agenda cost; disclose beside the Judgment Fund line in D4 tests.
